subject: SLO scope, measurement & reporting — next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@orionpay.com>, Tom Sullivan <tom.sullivan@orionpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO scope, measurement & reporting — next steps

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the SLA language:

Recap (on the performance side)
- Target use case: real-time payment risk scoring + short-form templated responses. Typical payload: 150-450 tokens generated; request rate average ~80 req/s with occasional bursts to 300 req/s.
- Key SLO asks from your side: P95 latency target, guaranteed concurrency, streaming for partial outputs, and monthly reporting (with incident notifications).

Open clarifying items (we need your confirmation)
1) Which metric matters most to you for end-user experience: server-side P95 (server processing only) OR end-to-end P95 (including network + client render)?
2) What are acceptable exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows, brief upstream routing spikes, expected cold-start period during scaled-up bursts?
3) Remedy expectation: credits only, or credits + root-cause report and technical remediation plan?

My proposed commitments (for discussion)
- Measurement: Redwood measures SLOs at the ingress/egress boundary of the serving cluster (server-side). We can provide optional synthetic E2E tests that run from your region and appear in the monthly report.
- Latency targets: two tiers we discussed — P95 < 200ms for single-shot generation; streaming initial-chunk latency (time to first token) P95 < 120ms for SSE/Chunked streams.
- Throughput/concurrency: Dedicated pool sizing commitment to handle sustained 120 req/s with burst-to-350 req/s for 15 minutes.
- Reporting cadence: monthly SLO dashboard export + immediate alert on any SLO breach with a 24-hour interim update and a 5-business-day RCA (if a breach > 5% over target).
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (we'll notify 72h in advance), third-party provider outages beyond Redwood control, customer-side throttling or malformed requests.

Next steps
- Elena / Tom: confirm whether you want server-side measurement only or E2E included in formal SLA.
- Ben / Karthik: we will circulate a redlineable SLA term doc by EOD (attaching a draft).
- Laura: can you prepare a short appendix describing how streaming metrics are logged (p95-first-byte, per-chunk latencies) to tuck into the SLA?

Attachments: redwood_slo_term_draft_v1.docx (first draft), orion_request_matrix.xlsx (your throughput/concurrency numbers)

Thanks — aiming to lock wording next week so procurement can start the legal review.

Best,
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: SLO scope, measurement & reporting — next steps

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap. A few answers and clarifications inline: 

1) Measurement: we prefer end-to-end P95 for any user-facing SLA item. We understand server-side is more precise for root cause, but legal wants the SLA tied to what our users experience. If Redwood provides both (server-side + synthetic E2E probes from our AWS region), that would work.

2) Exclusions: agreed on scheduled maintenance and third-party provider outages. We also want an exclusion for customer-driven spikes during major marketing campaigns (we'll provide expected campaign windows in advance). We need to avoid a maintenance window surprise that coincides with a campaign — 72h notice is fine.

3) Remedy: credits are primary. For enterprise, we also want a committed remediation plan: if there is a repeat breach (>2 occurrences in a rolling 90-day period), Redwood to provide prioritized engineering resources for a remediation plan and a timeline.

4) Reporting: monthly SLA dashboard export is good. We want a weekly summary email (even if green) while we’re in onboarding. After 3 months of steady operation we can step down to monthly.

5) Latency targets: the numbers you proposed look reasonable but confirm how you define "time to first token" for streaming — is it measured at the same ingress/egress boundary?

Tom and I will review the redline doc when you send it. Also please flag if any of our asks would require Dedicated vs Hosted (we currently expect Dedicated but want clarity on options).

Regards,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Engineering | OrionPay

Elena — thanks for the quick turn. Notes below and attached updated draft (v1.1) with the items you raised.

Answers / updates
- Measurement: we will record server-side metrics at the serving cluster boundary (ingress/egress) as authoritative for RCA, and run synthetic E2E probes from your primary AWS region for customer-facing SLA reporting. The SLA will reference E2E P95 as the user-facing metric and include a clause describing that RCA will rely on server-side metrics.
- Time-to-first-token (streaming): measured as timestamp delta between request arrival at ingress and the first byte emitted by the serving node (server-side). Our synthetic E2E probes will measure client-observed time-to-first-byte; both numbers will be visible in the monthly report.
- Exclusions: adding a customer-provided campaign window exclusion (must be announced 48h in advance to qualify). We will keep the 72h notice for planned maintenance.
- Remedies: amended draft includes tiered remedy language — service credits for single breaches; for repeat breaches (>=2 in a rolling 90-day period) Redwood will provide a prioritized remediation plan with a named engineering lead and a target remediation timeline (30 business days for P2/P1 items).
- Dedicated vs Hosted: the draft includes a short appendix that maps each committed throughput/concurrency target to configuration recommendations. Sustained 120 req/s with bursts to 350 req/s is within our Dedicated pool SLA; Hosted can support it but would require a short capacity ramp and different pricing. We'll flag the pricing delta in the commercial term sheet.

Action items
- Elena/Tom: review attached v1.1 and mark redlines to the E2E vs server-side clause and remedy language by EOD Tue 2026-06-02.
- Karthik: attach the streaming metrics appendix and a short note on how we run synthetic probes (region, frequency, agent).
- Laura: confirm who on support will own weekly onboarding summaries for first 90 days.

Attachments: redwood_slo_term_draft_v1.1.docx, streaming_metrics_appendix.pdf

If that looks good I'll push the revised doc to your procurement contact and create the HubSpot task for legal review.

Best,
